protocol.name: hyperdbdiag_dbmags_retrieve_contract_arbitrate_v10_epdg
protocol.llm_authority: may only choose between a hypergraph fallback and one candidate challenger; the direct ablation uses the training-OOF-sized top pair without local-judge decisions, while the complete method uses the locally retained structured-evidence pair; both require relation-specific stable positive grouped-OOF calibration and fail closed otherwise

hypergraph_training_selection.selection_policy: registered shared core defaults; no outer evaluation result used

epdg.root_metric_paths: registered mechanism paths plus stable signed root-metric paths learned from the current outer training fold
epdg.hypergraph_use: registered root-metric paths weight training hyperedge incidence; held-out query incidence uses no labels
epdg.cross_layer_paths: only frozen direct root-to-anonymous SQL/plan-shape atoms; raw SQL, identifiers, plans, and evaluation labels are excluded
epdg.fusion_selection: joint grouped inner-OOF selection with at least 0.01 absolute Exact gain required for nonzero EPDG fusion
epdg.unavailable_output: no SQL-template or execution-operator binding is emitted

protocol.ordinary_graph_training_selection: fixed shared baseline defaults inside each outer training split

evidence_eligibility.epdg_predictor_support: registered root-metric paths and direct anonymous runtime SQL-shape atoms
evidence_eligibility.llm_support: KPI-time trajectory, training-fold root profiles, anonymous SQL-shape atoms, and frozen mechanism cards
evidence_eligibility.excluded: raw SQL text, plans, source case IDs, scenarios, injection records, and evaluation labels
evidence_eligibility.reason: EPDG may use only registered direct anonymous SQL-shape paths; local and LLM review use the same bounded atoms plus training-grounded evidence.

protocol.local_structured_support: training-OOF-sized H candidate pool, group-balanced training profiles, frozen mechanism cards, and current anonymous semantic evidence when available; no evaluation labels, raw SQL, plans, source IDs, scenarios, or provenance
protocol.llm_structural_support: query KPI-time trajectory, anonymous SQL-shape atoms when available, outer-training root profiles, candidate-set topology, ECSA relation taxonomy, and frozen mechanism cards; local-judge runs may include two structured evidence cards, while the direct hypergraph-LLM run receives neutral candidate cards; no raw SQL, plans, source IDs, scenarios, case IDs, posterior values, candidate ranks, distances, or rarity
protocol.ordinary_graph_hypergraph_boundary: same KPI rows and labels only; no shared candidate inventory, decoder, fitted parameters, or output threshold
protocol.truth_access: evaluation labels are not passed to fit, evidence construction, prediction, or LLM calibration

stage.structure: fixed pairwise KPI graph with independent root-wise classifiers
signed-incidence higher-order hypergraph without EPDG path-prior fusion
stage.ablation_target: EPDG root-aware training incidence and direct anonymous SQL/plan path prior

stage.structure: signed-incidence higher-order hypergraph with EPDG path-prior fusion and joint root-set decoding
training-OOF-sized hypergraph pool plus local structured-evidence contraction
hypergraph top candidate-pair handoff with anonymous evidence and relation-aware LLM arbitration; no local structured-judge decision

steps: Review the reported predicate_type_conversion, filtered_relation_read, range_or_comparison_predicate, and row_locking_clause together.
Assess whether the conversion could make the predicate or join non-sargable, without inferring an unobserved access path.
Keep the row_locking_clause review separate from the observed lock-wait evidence; do not infer lock ownership.
preconditions: Use only the existing processlist/statement_history semantic observation; no SQL text, identifiers, or plan details are assumed.
Treat the correlated lock-wait metrics as one evidence family.
verification: Confirm the review produces only a bounded query-shape finding and supports any later human plan, index, or lock review decision.
Confirm that no statement, schema, session, or configuration state was changed.
rollback: No rollback is required; discard review notes without applying changes.

steps: Perform a read-only inspection of the execution-plan representation for the same anonymized runtime statement shape reported in observation-02.

Limit the review to whether the observed aggregation_clause and unrestricted_relation_read have plan evidence consistent with aggregation work and broad relation access; record findings for later human decision-making only.
Do not change SQL text, indexes, schema, sessions, locks, or configuration.
preconditions: The statement or statement shape being inspected must be the same one represented by observation-02.
Only non-mutating/read-only plan inspection or already-captured plan data is available.
No identifiers, SQL text, counts, or labels beyond the supplied evidence are assumed.
verification: Confirm the reviewed artifact corresponds to the observation-02 source channels: processlist or statement_history.
Check whether the inspection findings are consistent with mechanism-01 for group_by and mechanism-02 for missing_index without treating them as proof.
Preserve the finding as advisory evidence for a later human decision, not as an automatic remediation trigger.
rollback: No database rollback is required because the action is non-mutating.
If notes are incorrect, discard or amend the advisory record only.

steps: Perform a read-only plan inspection for the observed anonymous statement shape that includes an ordering_clause, filtered_relation_read, and range_or_comparison_predicate.
Use the inspection only to document whether the access path and ordering work are consistent with the frozen roots: missing_index and order_by.
Do not change indexes, query text, schema, sessions, or configuration as part of this step.
preconditions: A representative statement matching the semantic observation is available from the stated source channels.
The inspection method is non-mutating and does not execute destructive or state-changing work.
The frozen root set remains unchanged: missing_index and order_by.
verification: Confirm the inspected statement shape matches observation-02 before using the result.
Record the plan evidence relevant to filtered access and ordering work without adding unsupported identifiers or assumptions.
Use the result only to support a later human decision, not as proof by itself.
rollback: No rollback should be required because the action is read-only.
If any inspection approach would mutate state, stop and choose a non-mutating review instead.

steps: Review the current data-lock wait relationship evidence described in observation-01, focusing on whether a bounded waiter/blocker relationship is present.
Correlate that review with the contextual SQL-shape evidence in observation-02, specifically the presence of a row_locking_clause.
Use mechanism-02 as the validation frame: record_lock is supported by elevated lock-wait evidence and can coexist with independent query-work mechanisms.
preconditions: Limit the activity to read-only inspection/review of already available lock-wait and statement-shape evidence.
Do not terminate sessions, change transaction state, alter schema, or change configuration.
Treat correlated lock-wait metrics as one evidence family, as noted in observation-01.
verification: A later human decision is better supported if the review confirms an actual lock-wait relationship rather than only lock occupancy.
If no current wait relationship is present, record that the observed lock-wait spike may have been transient and do not infer an active blocker from occupancy alone.
Confirm that no state-changing action was taken during the review.
rollback: No database rollback is required because the recommended action is non-mutating.
If the review cannot be completed without state-changing actions, stop and discard any interim notes.

steps: Perform a read-only review of current data-lock wait relationships and related lock occupancy/session context to determine whether a record-lock wait chain is present now.
Treat correlated lock-wait metrics as one evidence family, and use the review only to validate whether later human remediation is warranted.
preconditions: Selected root set remains frozen as record_lock.
Use only existing read-only observability for current data-lock waits, current data-lock records, and active/non-sleeping session context.
Do not terminate sessions, change transaction state, restart services, or modify schema/configuration/data.
verification: Validate whether current lock-wait relationships exist or are absent at the time of review.
If relationships are present, confirm they are consistent with record_lock contention described by the mechanism card.
If relationships are absent, record that current direct wait evidence was not observed during this review.
rollback: No rollback is required for a read-only review.
Discard or archive review notes according to normal operational practice; no database state should have changed.

steps: Review the query shape for an overly large multi-table join and potential cardinality or join-work expansion, as described by mechanism-01.
Use observation-01 only as execution-pressure context; do not treat its lock metrics as proof of this root.
preconditions: The relevant query text or normalized query shape is available for human review.
The review is observation-only and will not execute or modify the query.
verification: Document whether the reviewed shape contains a multi-table join pattern consistent with increased cardinality and join work.
Confirm that no query, schema, lock, or configuration state was changed.
rollback: No rollback is required; discard review notes and apply no changes.

steps: Inspect available lock-wait relationships for the observed interval, prioritizing wait relationships over data-lock occupancy.
Correlate any available waiter and blocker context with existing processlist/statement-history records, including the observed row_locking_clause and multi_table_join shapes.
Record whether a concrete lock relationship supports the selected record_lock root without treating correlated wait metrics as separate evidence.
preconditions: Read-only access to current or retained lock-wait relationships and the supplied processlist/statement-history context.
A wait relationship from the observed interval remains available; otherwise historical validation is limited.
verification: The review is successful only if a concrete wait relationship and corresponding session context are observed.
If only data-lock occupancy is available, mark the result inconclusive because occupancy alone does not prove waiting or contention.
rollback: No rollback is required because this is inspection-only; discard any review notes without changing database state.

steps: Perform a read-only review of the representative statement or digest from the affected window to confirm whether an ordering clause is present and whether it plausibly aligns with the frozen `order_by` root.
preconditions: A representative query text, digest, or captured statement from the affected interval is available for read-only review.
Reviewer has permission to inspect query text/metadata without changing schema, data, configuration, or session behavior.
verification: Confirm whether the reviewed statement contains an ordering clause or other ordering-dependent query shape.
Relate the finding back to the observed workload/concurrency trajectory in observation-01 without treating those metrics as proof of the root cause.
rollback: No rollback is required because the action is inspection-only.
If the reviewed statement is not representative of the affected interval, discard the finding and request a representative read-only sample before making remediation decisions.

steps: Review the captured query-shape observation against the metric trajectory.
Treat aggregation_clause as direct semantic support for group_by.
Treat row_locking_clause as contextual support for record_lock, requiring the direct lock-wait evidence for contention assessment.
preconditions: Use only the existing processlist and statement_history observation; do not execute or modify statements.
Treat correlated lock-wait metrics as one evidence family, and do not treat data-lock occupancy alone as proof of contention.
verification: The review records whether the available shape evidence discriminates between the two frozen roots.
No SQL is executed and no database state is changed.
rollback: No rollback is required; discard the review notes if they are not useful.
Stop if validation would require execution or state change.

steps: Perform a read-only review of the existing lock-wait relationship evidence around the observed 15–30s elevation in the correlated lock-wait metrics.
Treat mysql_data_lock_waits and mysql_innodb_row_lock_current_waits as one correlated evidence family, not as separate confirmations.
Compare the lock-wait review with the supplied runtime SQL-shape observation showing row_locking_clause and aggregation_clause, documenting only whether these shapes co-occurred with wait evidence.
preconditions: Use only supplied current observations and captured source-channel metadata; do not require SQL text, identifiers, counts, or labels.
Keep the frozen root set unchanged: group_by and record_lock.
Do not perform writes, DDL, termination, restart, configuration, or index changes.
verification: Confirm the review notes cite the observed lock-wait trajectory and SQL-shape clauses.
Confirm record_lock interpretation is tied to direct lock-wait evidence from mechanism-02.
Confirm group_by remains represented only by the observed aggregation_clause mechanism from mechanism-01, without treating it as a lock primitive.
rollback: No database rollback is required because this is read-only.
If review notes exceed the supplied evidence, discard or mark those notes unsupported.

steps: Perform a read-only review of the anonymous statement shape captured in observation-02, focusing on the supplied predicate_type_conversion, filtered_relation_read, and range_or_comparison_predicate attributes.
Check whether the runtime predicate conversion described by mechanism-01 is actually present in the predicate or join comparison involved in that statement shape.
Review existing index applicability for the filtered relation and range/comparison predicate to inform whether the missing_index mechanism in mechanism-02 remains plausible for later human action.
preconditions: Use only metadata, statement-history/processlist context, or plan-inspection output already authorized for read-only review.
Do not change SQL text, schema, indexes, configuration, sessions, or locks.
Treat lock-wait metrics in observation-01 as contextual workload evidence only, not proof that either selected root is lock-based.
verification: Confirm whether the reviewed predicate contains a type conversion consistent with observation-02 and mechanism-01.
Confirm whether available index coverage appears applicable or absent for the filtered relation/range-comparison shape, consistent with mechanism-02.
Record the evidence used without introducing object names, SQL text, counts, or execution-plan details not present in the supplied observations.
rollback: No database rollback is required because the action is non-mutating.
Discard any temporary notes or derived review artifacts if they cannot be tied back to supplied evidence.

steps: Perform a read-only review of the already-captured query shape for the diagnosed workload, limited to predicates and joins.
Check only for evidence of runtime type conversion in a predicate or join, because this is the direct semantic signal for the frozen root implicit_conversion.
Treat the supplied metric trajectory as context only; do not infer lock contention or root confirmation from it alone.
preconditions: The reviewed artifacts must already exist or be obtained through an approved non-mutating diagnostic workflow.
The review scope must remain limited to the frozen root set: implicit_conversion.
No SQL changes, schema changes, configuration changes, restarts, or session terminations are performed.
verification: Confirm whether the reviewed predicate or join shape explicitly shows a runtime type conversion.
Record the artifact reference and whether predicate_type_conversion is present or absent for later human decision-making.
Do not double-count correlated lock-wait metrics as separate proof of this root.
rollback: No database rollback is required because the action is read-only.
If local review notes or annotations are incorrect, supersede or discard them without changing database state.

steps: Review already-available, read-only query-shape or statement-capture artifacts for the observed time window and mark whether any in-scope statements contain an aggregation_clause relevant to the frozen group_by root.
Compare any marked aggregation_clause occurrences with the general workload elevation shown in observation-01, especially mysql_threads_running at 30-60s and 60-75s.
Record the result as validation evidence only; do not change schema, terminate sessions, rewrite queries, or alter configuration.
preconditions: The selected root set remains frozen as group_by only.
Read-only query-shape or statement artifacts for the same observation window are already available.
The review is limited to inspection/documentation and does not execute or modify database state.
verification: A human reviewer can confirm whether aggregation_clause evidence is present or absent in the inspected artifacts.
The review notes cite mechanism-01 for why aggregation_clause is direct evidence for group_by.
The review notes cite observation-01 for the compatible workload-pressure context and avoid treating lock metrics as proof of the group_by root.
rollback: No database rollback is required because the action is non-mutating.
If the review scope or notes are incorrect, withdraw or correct the documentation only.

steps: Perform a read-only plan/query-shape inspection for the anonymous runtime statement shape described in observation-02.
